Field 64 at entrance 100. All refs are stock US bytes; the reconciler's listing is byte-identical to every reader's.

MAIN_INIT
- e0 t0 ip236 SWITCHEX takes the default (100) branch L402.
- ip408 sets the stage, Map.Byte[24]:=1.

- InitCode(4) ip434 and InitCode(3) ip437, then InitObject 5, 6, 13 (Zidane) and 20 (Blank) at ip440-449.

  - Then Wait(5), the 111 page (ip900), Wait(10), and the sync.

sword_fight.timing:
UNIT
- TimeLeft (Map.Byte[52]) is 50 at every arm (e20 t1 ip736). The :=30 at ip755 needs Int16[36]>0. Int16[36] is only ever set to 0 (e13 ip722/1010) or, if it is >=10, to 1 (e20 ip1515-1526), so that branch is dead.
- e3 t1 decrements it once per armed tick, the hit tick included (ip487-498). The loop ends in Wait(1) (ip506), and Wait(N) stores N-1 and yields (EBin.cs:1330-1361; ProcessCode decrements per pass, EBin.cs:136-158). So it is ONE decrement per FIELD EVENT TICK, never per render frame.
- FieldTPS is 30 (Memoria.ini:53), so a tick is 33.3 ms. FPSManager turns wall time into whole ticks (FPSManager.cs:77-111), so this holds at a ~31 or ~60 fps render.

ORDER WITHIN A TICK
- e3 runs before e20, so the arm tick S has already been polled.
- First poll: S+1. A press whose edge falls on tick S+j credits T=50-j, for j=1..50 (49 at most).
- At S+50 a pressless prompt reaches 0. e20 times it out in the same tick (ip1397-1424) and arms the next prompt in that same tick.
- A prompt lives 50 ticks, 1.67 s.

PASS LENGTH
- A pass lasts max(A, j). A is the reaction to the PREVIOUS result, and it plays while the new prompt is live: pass 0 is Wait(30); a LEFT/RIGHT hit is a 6-tick slide, a 7-frame clip and Wait(22), about 29 ticks; the others are 30-frame clips (anim_frames.json), with an extra tick when RunScript(2,13,11) waits for Zidane's previous tag 11.
- With fast answers a pass is about 30.5 ticks, so the fight is about 1525 ticks, about 51 s (estimate: the clips are assumed to play at one frame per tick). With no presses it is about 2480 ticks, about 83 s.
- After a hit the window closes on the hit tick and the next prompt opens about 25 ticks later, a visible gap. After a timeout the next prompt replaces it at once.

BEFORE THE FIGHT
- T0 is the tick e13's WindowSync wait sees 111 gone. That pass only clears the wait.
- e13 runs Wait(10) (ip906) at T0+1 and resumes at T0+11, when the Byte[26]/Bit[230] sync completes.
- e2 sets Byte24:=3 (ip134) at T0+12, and e20 arms the first prompt in that tick. The first poll is T0+13.

AROUND THE FIGHT
- Arrival to 105: 1.83 s (measured).
- 105/106: type-out of at most 250 ticks plus a press.
- 107/108: Wait(25) and Wait(37), the type-out, a press.
- Walk-off: about 2 s.
- Stage 6: pages and choice, about 5 s.
- Exit fade: Wait(65).

sword_fight.wrong_and_extra_presses:
WHAT KEYON IS
- B_KEYON (EBin.cs:1094-1101) is mask & ETb.KeyOn.
- ETb.ProcessKeyEvents (ETb.cs:50-56) sets sKeyOn = inputs & ~sKey once per tick, from EventEngine.ServiceEvents (EventEngine.cs:114-124).
- inputs = FPSManager.DelayedInputs (ETb.cs:58-63): the OR of the level reads of every frame since the last tick (FPSManager.cs:122-136, fed by EventInput.ReadInputLight -> ProcessInput(false,false), EventInput.cs:216-347).
- So a 1-frame tap lands on exactly one tick at 31 and 60 fps, and a held key gives one edge.
- EventInput.ReadInput, with its Chanbara branch (ProcessInput(true,true) & ChanbaraMask, :80-140), has NO caller in the clone. The HUD changes nothing on the input path.

WRONG BUTTON (any of the other seven bits in an armed tick)
- A MISS: Byte[47]:=3, Byte[46]:=10 or 11, sound 101, CloseWindow(1). The streak goes to 0 and the prompt ends at once.

TWO BUTTONS IN ONE TICK
- Always a miss. All eight checks run, and once Byte[46] is 10 or 11 even the right bit fails its compare.

START
- A held Start is a miss on every polled tick (B_KEY level, ip412). It is also the pause key: never press it.

BUTTONS NEVER READ
- L1/R1/L2/R2, Select and the logical-only bits do nothing.

PRESSES THAT ARE NOT POLLED (the edge is lost, harmlessly)
- Before the arm.
- Between prompts (Byte[47] != 1).
- On the arm tick itself: e3 polls before e20 arms.

PRESSES THAT ARE JUDGED
- A press while the PREVIOUS prompt is still armed is judged against that prompt.
- Consecutive prompts never repeat (e20 ip681), so pressing the last answered button again is ALWAYS a miss on the next prompt. A re-press of a lost press can land after the next arm, so it is a miss too: never re-press.

HELD BUTTON
- One edge. A key held across an arm gives no edge for the new prompt.

LATE PRESS
- At poll 50 the right button is still a hit, worth 0, and keeps the streak.
- After the timeout it falls on the next prompt, which cannot be the same button: a miss.

AFTER A REGISTERED PRESS
- The window closes on that tick, hit or wrong.
- [TIME=-1] sets FlagButtonInh (DialogBoxSymbols.cs:811-826), so Confirm never closes a prompt at the UI level. For the poll a Confirm is just the Cross bit.

OTHER STAGES
- Stages 2/4/8 read only logical Confirm (0x20000) or Special (0x80000) edges, and only after their INCS/250 gate.

REAL INPUT
- Real keyboard or pad input, including stick drift above the threshold (EventInput.cs:262-276), is OR-ed with the harness's. Unattended means hands off.

THE 100 PLAN: the harness driver scores a displayed 100/100 ("Of 100 nobles watching, / 100 were impressed.") in 64's sword fight, on both sides, every run.

0. SETTINGS (frozen in P-SETTINGS, never changed)
- Memoria.ini [Hacks] Enabled=1 and SwordplayAssistance=1 (:249, :252).
- FieldTPS=30 (:53).
- SwapConfirmCancel=0 (:127).
- A US session.
- The plan aims at a raw score of 100 or more. Its 100 does not depend on the engine's +30% (EMinigame.cs:18-19). It also means O4 cannot exercise that fork wrap.

1. WATCH
- The signal is state.json dialog.phrase_raw (State.raw_texts = Dialog.Phrase, the source with its tags; HarnessAgent.cs:1650-1656). The agent publishes it every 2nd frame (_stateEvery 2, :241, :1502).
- The rendered texts drop button glyphs (measured on O1's [CBTN] hint), so every prompt renders as "Press  !". Never key on texts.
- A PROMPT is a published dialog that meets all of these:
  - its phrase_raw holds exactly one [DBTN=(LEFT|RIGHT|UP|DOWN|CROSS|CIRCLE|TRIANGLE|SQUARE)], plus "Press" and "[TIME=-1]";
  - it is in place 64 (donor) at SC 1155;
  - control is off.
- 111, with eight DBTN tags, stays a page. 150's window 55, with two, is a stop page.
- A NEW INSTANCE is a prompt whose DBTN differs from the previous published prompt's, or one seen after a sample with no prompt. This works because consecutive prompts never repeat (64 e20 t1 ip681-691), and a timeout re-arms in the same tick.
- Poll in a tight loop (5-10 ms sleeps; a state read is about 0.2 ms) from the first prompt until 107/108 appear.
- Ride empty reads with Session._read_state (STATE_MISS_BUDGET 1 s).
- Keep the forbidden scan and every wait_frames out of this loop.
- Optional: `stateevery 1` for the fight, which halves the publish lag. The agent resets it on re-arm.

2. PRESS
- Exactly ONE `press <name> 2` per instance, blocking for its ack.
- The map:

| Prompt | Press |
|---|---|
| LEFT | `left` |
| RIGHT | `right` |
| UP | `up` |
| DOWN | `down` |
| TRIANGLE | `menu` |
| CROSS | `confirm` |
| CIRCLE | `cancel` |
| SQUARE | `special` |

- The physical bits come from EventInput.GetKeyMaskFromControl (EventInput.cs:476-534) through logicalToButton, the identity when cfg.control==0 and the layout is not JP (HonoInputManager.cs:967-981). Directions are set directly in ProcessInput.
- NEVER `circle`: HarnessAgent.cs:1434 maps it to Control.Confirm, the Cross bit, which misses.
- Never Start: held, it is a miss every tick (64 e3 t1 ip412).
- Never two buttons. Nothing between instances.
- No re-press: a lost press is a VOID. A re-press can land after the next arm, and that is a certain miss, because the next prompt is never the same button.
- Rule 7 (the page rule) never presses while a prompt is published. The driver records prompt rows, not pages, so the transcript stays comparable across random sequences.

3. BUDGET, IN FIELD TICKS (33.3 ms)
- e3 polls before e20 in every tick (Obj.cs:31-45; EBin.cs:106-160). So a prompt armed at tick S (64 e20 t1 ip721/736) is first polled at S+1.
- A press whose edge lands on tick S+j is credited T = 50-j. It must land by j=50. At S+50 the prompt times out (e20 t1 ip1397-1424).
- 100 under the live SA 1 needs the 50 credits (the 49 hits plus the phantom's repeat of T_49) to sum to at least 1066. A uniform j of 28 or less does it: j=28 gives raw 80, then 104, then 100.
- The plan's own target is assist-independent: a sum of at least 1675, a uniform j of 16 or less.
- MEASURED LATENCY (archives; request write to agent acceptance):

| Render rate | Median | p99 | Max | Presses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 fps | 54 ms | 78-85 ms | 100-122 ms | 2002 (story-o2, story-o3) |
| 30 fps | 72 ms | 126-133 ms | 145-171 ms | 369 |

- Add 0-2 frames of publish lag and the frame+1 press schedule. That gives j of about 3-5 typical and at most about 8-11 at the worst seen.
- So the raw score is about 114-123, and the displayed score is 100 with or without the bonus.
- Margins:
  - about 40 ticks to the per-prompt timeout;
  - about 24 ticks of mean to SA 1's line;
  - about 12 ticks of mean to SA 0's line.
- An empty state read of up to 200 ms costs about 6 ticks on one prompt.
- The only fatal event is a stall of about 1.4 s or more on one armed prompt.

4. AROUND THE FIGHT (all proven machinery)
- Rule 7 handles 105/106: repeated Confirm until the script's KEYON closes them. The loop at e13 t1 ip865-885 starts only after SYSVAR[8]>=2 or 250 ticks, and earlier presses are lost.
- Rule 7 also handles the 111 page, 107/108 (ip1404), and pages 122, 123 and 128.
- The frozen choice rule {donor 64, sc [1155], match "No", pick "No", once: true} answers 127 with g.choose(1). The cursor opens on Yes (0); never take the default.
- After 111 leaves the dialog list (T0), the first prompt arms at T0+12 and is first polled at T0+13.
- No Confirm edge may land at T0+13 or later. The script and the agent read the same dialog list (MesWinActive = CheckDialogShowing, DialogManager.cs:176-182). So a rule-7 press decided while 111 is still published lands within about 3-6 ticks of T0. The analysis checks this from the press rows.

5. EVIDENCE
- One `prompt` row per instance:
  - n (1-49), the DBTN, the button sent;
  - the first frame and time it was published;
  - the request seq, the accepted frame, and the down frame (accepted + 1);
  - the first frame without it;
  - j bounds in ticks from g.rate(), and the render regime.
- Plus O3's page, choice and press rows.

6. HOW THE SESSION PROVES THE 100: a new check, O4-SWORD, on every covered run of both sides
- (a) Exactly one trace row 64 e4 t1 ip338 Global.Byte[475] 0 -> 100, and exactly one ip390 Global.Bit[3815] 0 -> 1 (S fld 64, F fld member(64)).
- (b) The published pages "Of 100 nobles watching,\n100 were impressed." (mes 122, e4 t1 ip375), then "Queen Brahne was\nquite impressed." (123, ip384). No 120/121 ("Of the 100 ..." / "not impressed").
- (c) Choice 127 ("They demand an encore!") answered No, once.
- (d) Page 128 "They shower you with 10000 Gil!" ([NUMB=1] is 10000 only at a score of 100, ip296-307).
- (e) 49 prompt rows, one mapped press each, every j in its bound, each window gone after its press.
- (f) No other press between the first prompt and 107.
- O4-WRITES, NULL and STATE then compare the 26 keys as O3 did.

7. ON A MISS: a VOID of its own class, never a FAIL by itself
- A score below 100 changes Byte[475] and/or drops Bit[3815]. It does so because the driver's INPUT changed, not because the scripts under test did. A run whose input is not the frozen play is no sample of the claim.
- V17 (driver, new). Any of these:
  - a prompt still published about 50 ticks after it was first seen (a timeout);
  - an instance with no press, two presses, or a wrong name;
  - a press outside an instance in stage 3;
  - a score page other than 122 with 100.

  The driver stops at once. end_run (warp 4600, then soft reset) recovers; R-CHANBARA-VOID proves this from 64. The run is re-run (rerun.max 2), as O3 did for V15.
- V18 (game, new; a FINDING, in rerun.stop_on). The driver's 49 rows prove the frozen play: one mapped press per instance, every j in budget, each window gone on its own press. The game still showed 120/121 or a score below 100. VOID-ASYM reads it:
  - on one side only, NOT PROVEN: the fork scores or reads input differently;
  - in every run of both sides, NOT PROVEN: the instrument, e.g. a remapped pad.
- A Yes is V2 (the `once` rule).

8. CHANGES
- Engine, agent, harness verbs: NONE. The prompt is published (phrase_raw). Presses reach B_KEYON: harness -> HonoInputManager.IsInput -> UIKeyTrigger.GetKey -> ProcessInput(false,false) -> FPSManager collect/flush -> ETb.ProcessKeyEvents -> B_KEYON. O1-O3 proved Confirm -> KEYON and held Up -> B_KEY. The trace sees both keys.
- An agent instrument that publishes Dialog.TextId or Map.Byte[47]/[52]/Int16[42] would give per-prompt hit/miss evidence. But it needs a DLL rebuild, and that AUTO-DEPLOYS over the live install (build_memoria.py backs up; owner-gated). It is not worth it for O4.
- Driver, opt-in pred["chanbara"], checked strict like movies_of; O1-O3 stay byte-identical without it (segment_regress G1-G14):
  - the prompt rule, before rule 7;
  - the button map, with a test that `circle` FAILS on a CIRCLE prompt;
  - the prompt rows;
  - V17/V18;
  - the 127 choice rule;
  - an o4 checks module: O4-SWORD; P-SETTINGS with SwordplayAssistance; P-DONOR requiring `<member(64)> 64`; P-LAUNCH after the alxc deploy.

9. FAKEGAME MUST MODEL
- Field 64 at entrance 100, and member(64).
- Stage 1, about 1.8 s.
- 105/106: [INCS][TIME=-1], an INCS/250-tick gate, then a KEYON loop. The 111 page.
- 50 passes and 49 prompts with every e20 filter: SByte[38]; max-combo 10 and 15; Circle -> Triangle and Square -> Cross; no repeat. Seedable.
- The arm and the window in one tick. The reaction (about 29-31 ticks) overlapping the live prompt. First poll at S+1.
- TimeLeft 50, decremented every armed tick including the hit tick. A timeout at poll 50 that re-arms in the same tick.
- Per-tick KEYON edges of the harness's held buttons for the 8 bits, plus held Start and two keys in one tick.
- The Control -> bit map, so `circle` misses.
- Publication: texts "Press  !" and phrase_raw with the DBTN. Confirm does not close a prompt. A configurable close tween.
- Exact scoring:
  - the phantom pass, /29;
  - the +30% at SA 1, with a knob for whether it fires on member(64);
  - SA 2's refill;
  - the clamp and the gil.
- Trace rows ip338/ip390.
- Pages 120/121 versus 122/123, with [NUMB].
- Choice 124-127 with the cursor on 0. Yes replays (110/109 plus KEYON, no tutorial). No gives 128 plus AddGil.
- 107/108, and the exit to 150 at 325.
- Faults:
  - a publish stall, or a driver stall over an armed prompt;
  - a lost press, a double press;
  - a key held across an arm;
  - a stray Confirm after 111.

10. REHEARSALS (stock, before the freeze)
- R-CHANBARA (`warp 64 100 1155`, ends at Field(150), x2). It measures:
  - the prompts' phrase_raw and texts;
  - that a 49/49 run reads 122/123/127/128 (this proves the eight buttons and cfg.control);
  - j per prompt, and the close tween;
  - T0 against the first prompt;
  - 127's options and selected;
  - the fight's length.
- R-CHANBARA-VOID: stop mid-fight; end_run must reach the title.
- R-FULL (64 -> 153, x2): the 26 keys, the end state, the run time and the budgets.
- Optional, owner's call, not in the session: R-CHANBARA-GATE. A paired S/F run at a fixed j of about 20 (raw 93). There S reaches 100 only through the +30%, so an F that shows 93 would expose the EMinigame wrap.

11. HANDS OFF
- Real input is OR-ed with the harness's. A key, a pad press or stick drift during stage 3 is a press.
- Every perfect run also reports the Encore achievement to Steam. That is outside gEventGlobal, but the owner should know.

problems.evidence:
Rule 7 presses again while the same page text is still listed. A closing page stays listed for its close tween (DialogAnimator.cs:213 sets 0.15 s, about 4.5 ticks; ReleaseDialogToPool at DialogManager.cs:269-274).

The gaps, verified:

- choice 127 opens at T0'+11 (e4 t1 ip384, then ip390, Wait(10) at ip399, then ip462).

A press decided while the page is still listed lands up to about 8 ticks later: publish of 2 frames or less, accept up to 171 ms, then frame+1. That leaves only about 3-5 ticks of margin.

A stray on 127 takes the default, Yes (cursor 0), and replays the fight. pick_for then raises V2 attributed by="game" (segment_drive.py ~158-161), so a one-sided stray reads as a false NOT PROVEN. O4 is the first segment where a non-default pick follows a page.

GO: design O4 from this map, once the two majors are folded in:
1. Per-side end handling, since F ends in member(153), not in a real field.
2. A decision on witnessing the +30% wrap. A paced mean j of about 22 ticks still scores 100/100 on both sides.

The map's core holds; I re-derived each item below from the bytes, engine and harness code:

THE SWORD FIGHT
- **Score formula:** 64 e4 t1 ip208, (I30+I32)/29, then the +30% at sid 4 ip 223, then the clamp at ip222-233.
- **Phantom 50th credit:** e20 ip710 skips the arm, so the 49th result is credited again (I32 = 1225, max combo 50).
- **100 under SwordplayAssistance 1:** needs raw >= 79, i.e. I30 >= 1066 or a uniform j of 28 or less. Memoria.ini:249/252.
- **TimeLeft unit:** one decrement per tick, only while armed and on the hit tick too (e3 t1 ip487-498 inside the Byte[47]==1 block). Field ticks run at 30/s (FieldTPS :53), with FastForwardFactor reset to 1 on New Game.
- **Tick order:** e3 polls before e20 in each tick (Obj.cs tail append), so the first poll is S+1 and T = 50-j.
- **Input path:** level reads are OR-ed per tick (FPSManager.cs:122-136) and the edge is taken in ETb.cs:50-56. ReadInput's Chanbara branch is dead (its only callers are absent).
- **Prompt visibility:** a prompt joins activeDialogList in its own arm tick (DialogManager.cs:200).
- **Button map:** confirm/cancel/menu/special give the Cross/Circle/Triangle/Square bits. The 'circle' alias is the Confirm trap.
- **Wrong, double or late presses:** behave as described.
- **Latency budget:** realistic j is about 4-6 ticks typical and 11 or less worst, giving raw 114-119 or more.
- **Encore choice:** the cursor opens on Yes (WindowSync flags 0 resets sChoose to 0).

ROUTE AND START
- **No control in 64:** mapvar is cleared at field start (EventEngine.cs:625-626), so Map.Bit[158] = 0 and no EnableMove.
- **150:** stage 10 is deterministic.
- **End:** candidate 2 is the right end.

FORK CHAIN

- **Donors:** no alxc donor is in ForkDonorPatch, and no stack override touches 64/150/153.
- **Text blocks:** block 3 is unshipped; block 2's us == uk copy (md5 ddf99c96ea = sha256 3a6f3246c2, the same file) will be rewritten by the deploy.
